newsitem.title: USA: Captive insurance market increased in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Captive insurance market increased in 1996.

text.p: The number of captive insurance companies worldwide increased by about 200 in 1996 to a nearly 3,800, according to risk management consultants Tillinghast-Towers Perrin.
According to the firm's 1997 Captive Insurance Company Directory, there are 3,795 captive insurers with worldwide annual premiums estimated at $19 billion.
Captive insurance companies are special purpose insurance vehicles formed by large companies or groups to insure their own or related risks.

"In the past year, a lot of dust was stirred up by some people saying that the captive movement was past its prime and about to go into reverse," said Hugh Rosenbaum, a Tillinghast-Towers Perrin principal and editor of the firm's Captive Insurance Company Reports.
"The growth figures for 1996 show that nothing of the sort has started to happen," he said.
Total captive capital to surplus is at the $45 billion mark, while assets are estimated to be about $100 billion worldwide.
Although the 1996 insurance market remained soft, many new U.S.-sponsored single-owner captives continued to be formed, the firm said.
In Europe, the upward trend in new captive formation continued from the previous year, the firm said.
"Captive business is big business," Rosenbaum said.
